description:
FILED s543n (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) while measuring #513 (the fdopen alias's own buffer).  PRE-EXISTING (base 617d66c8 = the s543n tree).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL; STDOUT a pipe or a file, no $|):
    print "1 STDOUT\n";
    open(my $k, ">&", \*STDOUT) or die; print $k "2 via dup\n"; print "3 STDOUT\n";
    open(my $j, ">&", \*STDOUT) or die; print $j "4 via dup2\n"; print "5 STDOUT\n";
    perl: 1 3 4 2 5      PCL: 1 3 5 2 4
(each dup open flushes STDOUT -- right in both; then perl's global destruction frees the file-scoped lexicals newest
first, flushing $j then $k, and PerlIO_cleanup flushes STDOUT last; PCL's exit hook writes STDOUT before the rest.)
Any two handles sharing a descriptor or a file show it: a `>&` dup, an `>&=` alias once it has its own buffer (#513),
two `>>` opens of one log file.  Probe: the s543n worktree's scratch/s543n/probes/pF3.pl.  The exit hook's order is
the place (the flush of every open output stream at exit, docs/ir-spec.md 6.5b); #513's alias buffer depends on it.
frequency_reason: the order of two buffered handles on one descriptor at exit (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): at exit PCL writes STDOUT's buffer FIRST and then the other buffered handles in creation order -- perl frees the lexical handles first, newest first, then flushes STDOUT: two handles on one descriptor (a `>&` dup of STDOUT) come out in a different order
triage_reason: a silent wrong of output ORDER at exit when two buffered handles share a descriptor or a file: IN (rare)
